note: Reference-standard-driven executable check (Roberts: numerical statement MEANINGFUL iff truth value invariant under every admissible scale transformation) applied to corpus epistemic formulas; grounds 07-MEASUREMENT-THEORY-GAP.md.
A corpus-proposed evidence-aggregation formula, executed and shown unbounded, non-idempotent, dimensionally undefined.

A corpus-proposed evidence-independence formula, executed and shown to conflate dependency-graph depth with statistical independence (assigns a verbatim copy the same weight as an independent observation).
Four defensible definitions of assertion-membership-in-K and state-equality K1=K2 that disagree on the same test cases, executed against a reference kernel; grounds 12-IDENTITY-EQUALITY-GAP.md.

Whether KnowledgeOS state-merge forms an algebra (idempotent/commutative/associative) depends on which conflict-resolution rule is chosen; exhaustive search executed for two candidate rules (conflict-marking, latest-wins).

The unresolved question of which competence/authority binds to which policy gate; Authorize is shown to be a signature without a body, with no AuthorityAct type and three concrete counterexamples (revocation, policy-version mismatch, authority-less execution).

notations: SUFFICIENT: Evidence x Context x Constitution -> {True,False,Unknown}
note: A DeepSeek-sourced (non-incorporated) principle that sufficiency is constitution-dependent; shown to fail for constitutions requiring relational sufficiency (independence/corroboration) because Evidence declares no independence relation.
Measured overload of core symbols E, V and especially Omega (at least four global senses, two foundational and mutually inconsistent in direction), contradicting a prior claim that UL was closed.

Measured 132/132 humanActRef non-empty across the estate is shown to prove only that a free-text field is always filled, not that authority is bound; the ladder_dc_reference.py witness proving Sigma-perp-Gamma is shown to be a tautological null-check (evidence_volume parameter never read); the ratified canonical-architecture-v0.2 (I-11, R-1 stratification) already closes the underlying question by a different, unreconciled mechanism.

The finding that K=(A,R) is empirically instantiated by the real Engineering Knowledge Platform document graph, not by PublicDigit's election domain as Step 267 assumed -- a Type-1 semantic realization Step 267 missed by searching the wrong system.

Empirical confirmation that the EKP's status and authority axes vary independently (7 observed pairs vs 5x5 max), already schema-declared as independent; but neither axis is the theory's Sigma (epistemic support) and no field in the running system records whether a claim is supported by evidence.

knowledge-lint.php is measured to emit 16 distinct rule identifiers covering structure (referential integrity, cycles, single-authoritative, orphans) but none for status-transition legality or evidence/epistemic support.

A typed uncertainty object surviving all five tested placements for uncertainty (in Assertion, in Evidence, as a relation, as an external annotation, as a probability distribution) that the audit had declared inexpressible; its update/merge algebra is undefined and it overlaps unreconciled with Sigma=(dir,str).

A formal, typed, quantified identifiability definition over a world-space W and observation function Omega, requiring KnowledgeOS to be able to return 'Underdetermined'; distinguishes Underdetermined (resolvable by more data) from Non-identifiable (an information-theoretic limit, never resolvable) -- a distinction the audit's single label collapsed.

notations: not assessed / absent / not applicable / unresolved
note: Two independent corpus constructions (a six-way Zero-taxonomy with five non-collapse laws, and a Navya-Nyaya-derived Abhava ontological absence typology with an AbsenceClaim record shape) together covering seven of eight mandate-listed missingness cases; identifies D_t, the recognised-dimension set, as the smallest component missing from K=(A,R) needed to make 'not assessed' decidable.

A domain-space/epistemic-space separation argued in kernel/20260825-184755 as preventing a universal-filtering-regime illusion, abandoned by the corpus after 2026-08-26 (finding EV-A2) and re-admitted here because the argument for it was never rebutted, only forgotten.

An executed, per-edge-sourced definitional dependency graph over ~26 KnowledgeOS terms (Observation, Entity, Proposition, Evidence, Assertion, K, Policy, Authority, Governance, etc.), tested for cycles via Tarjan SCC and for transitive dependence on non-computable (class-C) objects.

Step 266's named set of objects with no decision procedure (Relevance, Truth, Adequacy, Authority, Assessment, EpistemicStatus, Minimality, Policy), used here as the sink set for a transitive-blockage analysis over the dependency graph.

Authority is measured to carry four distinct senses (competence relation, 7-ary function, actor-standing rank, and EKP artifact trust-grade), three separated by a prior audit but the fourth (a document's trust grade, different subject of predication -- artifact not actor) left unhandled; recorded as TG-07.

Assurance is measured to have at least five live, mutually incompatible definitions in the corpus despite being already REFUTED as definable under a prior finding CB-1, yet remaining in active use -- called 'the worst term in the corpus'.

notations: pi1 == pi2 (behavioral equivalence relative to O_A,O_T)
note: Step 271's central hypothesis (H_271, explicitly not a theorem): KnowledgeOS should define Policy and Assessment at the semantic-interface level only, leaving internal rule/measurement regimes external and pluggable unless corpus evidence forces a universal internal structure; includes a semantic (behavioral, operation-set-relative) equivalence for policies, distinct from textual equality.

notations: KnowledgeOS Core vs External semantic regimes
note: A proposed architectural boundary listing Knowledge State/Assertion/Relation/Identity/History/Transformation-interface/Evidence-interface/Assessment-interface/invariants as core, versus policy rules/measurement models/statistical models/domain thresholds/assessment criteria/governance rules as external regimes; explicitly a hypothesis pending corpus audit confirmation.

A proposed (not yet established) orthogonality test between epistemic assessment status and governance/administrative status, illustrated by a proposition that is epistemically well-supported but administratively rejected; framed as needing corpus confirmation, feeding into Step 272's Sigma derivation.

Representing 'value unknown' requires either widening every value-space V_D with a bottom element or a new carrier type; neither is defined in the canonical theory, so an unknown proposition value cannot be constructed without inventing a definition.
N (the Knower) is used in Authorize's signature but never defined as a space, with no identity criterion or equality, making 'the same authority act' inexpressible.

Since Gamma (governance/commitment status) is derived rather than a component of K, delta(K,e) has nowhere in K to write a commit result, leaving the state transition for the system's central governed act formally undefined.
Sarathi is measured to have a 7-ary signature with no body anywhere in the corpus, listed as one of eight construction gap points.

notations: Kernel enforces authority claims; Kernel does not originate authority
Authority subset Actor x Action x Context x Time
note: Step 187's normative (not mathematical) decision that Authority is exogenous to the kernel, breaking the Assertion->Evidence->Rule->Policy->Authority->Assertion definitional cycle at the architecture level while its own recorded normative/provenance basis B re-enters the cycle at the representation level; makes every theorem about K conditional on an unspecified external authority oracle.

Context (c/C) occurs in the two most load-bearing definitions in the theory (Assertion and the Evidence relation) with no declared domain, equality, ordering, composition rule, or relation to the EKP's bounded_context field anywhere in the corpus, and has no row in Step 266's audit table; makes Evidence(O,P,C1,R)=Evidence(O,P,C2,R)? unanswerable.

A disciplined, ID-numbered (TG-01..TG-21) consolidated gap register with an explicit rule: no proposal unless a corpus search for an existing resolution returned nothing; distinguishes OPEN, CORPUS RESOLVES-NOT-ADOPTED, BLOCKING, and NEW-in-this-pass dispositions across 21 gaps spanning mathematical/semantic/computational/empirical/governance classes.

notations: (a) different ontology (b) equivalent (c) conservative extension (d) incomparable (e) contradictory
note: A classification of all 28 corpus-wide K definitions (from 01-THEORY-EVOLUTION-MAP.md ARC B) into five relationship classes, finding only 10/28 reconcilable as equivalent or conservative-extension, 11 incomparable, 3 different ontologies, and 1 (Q7's JTB knowledge-atom K=(A,J,T_A)) a category error sharing a symbol with every state-valued K.

An argument, using Step 260's own K*=H/== definition, that K has no intrinsic content -- its content is entirely determined by the mandatory operation set O -- so treating K as an ontology (a claim about what knowledge IS) rather than a representation (a sufficient statistic for a chosen O) is what produced the proliferation of 28 tuples; reframes the disagreement as downstream of a missing operation registry.

notations: K=(A,R) sufficient iff O excludes history-sensitive predicates
note: Executed demonstration (exp_congruence.py EXP-3) that two histories with different contestation trajectories (H_calm vs H_stormy) reach a byte-identical K=(A,R), so K is sufficient only if the mandatory operation set excludes history-sensitive predicates like ever_contested (an ordinary governance predicate the corpus's own Steps 155/179/181 discuss); concludes the widely-repeated claim 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient knowledge state' is not a corpus theorem but a consequence of an unstated choice of O.

A mandate-required refusal to collapse theory closure into a single PASS/FAIL verdict; instead scores eight distinct senses of closure separately (1 NO mathematically, 2 NO semantically, 3 PARTIAL computationally, 4 NO empirically, 5 PARTIAL implementation-conformant, 6 PARTIAL governance-closed, 7 PARTIAL practically implementable, 8 NO theoretically complete), each with named decisive evidence.

A dependency-ordered list of six missing concepts, concluding that (W,Omega) -- the world and the observation function, 'the referent of knowledge itself' -- is the single smallest missing concept, since everything else (non-identifiability, D_t's dimension semantics, Qualify's semantics, and K's adequacy being scorable-only-not-judgeable) depends on it; two of the six (W,Omega and D_t) require only adoption of already-existing corpus material, not invention.

An independent, md5-verified, read-only book-production acceptance review of Part II (chapters II.1-II.4) of KnowledgeOS book Edition 2, commissioned GN-68 and receipted GN-69, following a correction pass GN-67; verdict ACCEPT WITH CORRECTIONS conditioned on fixing one RED defect (a stale word-count creating two contradictory artifact identities).

An executed classification of ten corpus-required example propositions against the terminal type P=(Entity,Dimension,Value): finds negation, conditional determination, and quantification INEXPRESSIBLE; validity-interval and units LOSSY; assertion-level contradiction NOT-A-PROPOSITION (expressed as an R-edge instead, with no stated relationship between the two content mechanisms); and epistemic-Unknown AMBIGUOUS between a value-space entry and assertion absence.

'Claim' is used throughout the corpus (claim registry, authority claims, claim provenance) and even has a dedicated section (Step 253 §253.14) discussing it, yet is never given a type, identity criterion, or stated relation to Assertion; recommended repair is retiring the word as a synonym for Assertion rather than defining it as a new concept.

The terminal Assertion type carries a single temporal field t, but the corpus separately establishes bitemporality (T_valid != T_known, Steps 185 and 025w); Step 187's own worked example (a board-chair role with a validity interval) needs a validity interval the type cannot hold, so either t is assertion-time (validity unrepresentable) or validity-time (replay loses its ordering key).

notations: R subset A x A x RelType
note: The theory carries propositional content via two unreconciled mechanisms: P for entity-dimension-value facts and R for inter-assertion facts (e.g. contradicts), with R-edges being bare triples carrying no id, evidence, provenance, or status -- yet R_der is shown elsewhere (exp_congruence.py EXP-2) to be exactly the load-bearing component that makes the state sufficient.

Unknown fits neither the value space (a category error per Step 264's own 'Nexus Version problem' warning) nor absence-of-assertion (indistinguishable from never-having-asked, destroying the corpus's own Zero concept per 025d); since sigma is not a field of the terminal Assertion type, Unknown currently has nowhere to live.

A vocabulary-independent necessity test: ten constructed situations are checked against nine theory-required downstream decisions to derive how many distinct status values and axes are mathematically necessary, finding at least five orthogonal irreducible facts (asked, evidence, authority, supersession, validity) plus a sixth unmodeled fact (an open contest process) -- refuting any single-axis or naive single-enum Sigma.

A sixth Sigma requirement surviving decomposition into five orthogonal axes: distinguishing 'one supporting item' from 'meets the policy bar' requires an evidential-sufficiency-relative-to-a-declared-bar value (Insufficient) distinct from Unknown and Supported; independently converged upon by zero_reference.py's PF-1 finding that the ratified four-arm status summary has no arm for Insufficient, Stale, or Prohibited.

Contested is argued to be a fact about an open challenge process (with its own lifecycle: opened/adjudicated/withdrawn and duration) rather than a property of an assertion's evidence/authority/supersession/validity; forcing it into a single status enum produces the corpus's own documented PF-6 inexpressibility ('Accepted AND Contest:Active' has no single-state representation), reframed here as evidence the enum shape is wrong rather than a tolerable residue.

Candidate is used ambiguously for both 'not enough evidence yet' (evidence axis) and 'not yet accepted by an authority' (authority axis), which the five-axis decomposition shows are different states with different remediation paths (gathering evidence vs an authority act) and which EXP-23 shows must not collapse.

Closure-04's Evidence(O,P,C,R) relation (2026-08-27) is well-formed and argued soundly, but its load-bearing Relevant predicate is separately classified by Step 266 (three days/240 steps later) as class C (no decision procedure); no document in the corpus cross-references the two, making the qualification rule well-formed and non-computable without either side noticing -- named the most common failure mode found across the whole corpus: correct local results that are never composed.

The deepest measurement-theory finding: Roberts' framework has four stages (empirical structure, representation, scale, meaningful operations); the corpus imports only the third and fourth (assigning scale types and admissible transformations) and never executes the first -- no observable relation like 'a is at least as well supported as b' is ever shown to satisfy the axioms (weak order, solvability, Archimedean for higher scales) that would license any numerical representation of an epistemic quantity at all.

A grep-based census over the primary corpus finds 45 distinct right-hand-side strings and 11 named transition functions (T, T_t, T_K, Update, Revise, Revision, Recalculate, Derive, Transition, Learn, Improve) plus several unnamed forms, with arities ranging from 1 to >=6; the most-repeated form K_{t+1}=delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t) contains two symbols (rho, Omega) with no declared type anywhere in the corpus.

The first executable KnowledgeOS transformation kernel built in the entire research programme: a total, deterministic, replayable T over a four-operation set (assert, relate, withdraw, restatus) with cascading withdrawal over derives edges; verified to have no preconditions, no postconditions, and no invertibility (withdraw is destructive).
'Verdict' is used throughout Step 240, Step 266, and the whole review programme without ever being typed -- the same undefined-term defect class as Claim (05-ASSERTION-SEMANTICS.md CS-1).

Authority (a standing, time-indexed relation) and Authorization (a dated act) are explicitly distinguished by Step 187 §187.1 but then used interchangeably from Step 190 onward, despite Authority being time-indexed while an authorization act is a point event that must be separately recorded.

notations: authorities.yaml, statuses.yaml, etc. 0 knowledge cards each
note: All ten schema vocabulary files in the EKP (authorities.yaml, statuses.yaml, bounded-contexts.yaml, etc.) carry zero knowledge cards -- no knowledge_id, status, authority, owner, or review date -- and are not validated by knowledge-lint as documents, meaning an edit to any of them silently changes the meaning of every governed document with no ADR, review, owner, or lint gate; the one designed defense (knowledge-lint's S3 declared-vocabulary check) is 132/132 INCONCLUSIVE because its required config file schema/vocabulary-integrity.yaml does not exist, though its fail-closed design (INCONCLUSIVE rather than false PASS) is praised while the overall structural-profile mechanism is noted as warn-only, wired into no gate, and exits 0.

An executed placement matrix determining, test by test, which provenance/lineage/history-related questions are answerable from K=(A,R) alone: assertion provenance and lineage (via R_der reachability) are answerable; transition provenance, merge provenance, withdrawal record, contestation record, evidence provenance, and source-independence are all NOT answerable from K alone.

The corpus's most-repeated implementation claim ('provenance/lineage is realized in production, GovernanceLineageGraph, 47 tests', cited in >=15 verification artifacts) is reproduced exactly via php artisan test --filter=Lineage (47 passed, 125 assertions across 18 test classes), but only one class (GovernanceLineageGraphTest, 4 tests) actually exercises the typed provenance graph; the other 43 tests merely share the substring 'Lineage' in unrelated class names (membership-lifecycle, voting-eligibility, election-security). The underlying claim is true but its evidential weight is ~12x overstated in 14 downstream artifacts that propagated the round number.

notations: Step 267 semantic-realization taxonomy: Type 1 vs Type 3
note: GovernanceLineageGraph lives in App/Contexts/Membership/Domain/Committee/Constitutional/Lineage, the election platform's committee-governance context; under Step 267's own semantic-realization taxonomy this is Type 3 (analogy: a decision-lineage graph for committee governance that happens to share the theory's shape), not Type 1 (genuine semantic realization); Step 267 §267.5 explicitly states Type 3 must not be reported as implementation, yet Step 267's own evidence table reports this exact class as IMPLEMENTED + 47 tests.

Of the mandate's six required identity criteria, only assertion identity (partially, via id) and version identity (IMPLEMENTED only in the EKP, not in the theory) exist; evidence identity, knowledge-state identity, transformation identity, and policy identity are all absent from the theory, and Step 266's own stated dependency (deterministic replay requires operation versioning) is therefore unsatisfied since no transformation identity exists.

A sharpening of Step 260's own premises (equivalence defined by universal quantification over an unenumerated operation set T, decidability marked UNRESOLVED at 260.15): since T has no extension, the equivalence relation is not merely undecidable but UNCONSTRUCTED (a relation defined by a quantifier ranging over an open collection is not yet a relation); traces a five-link dependency chain by which K*, A-in-K membership, K1=K2 state equality, the Step 259 sufficiency theorem, and Step 266's minimality marking all inherit this unconstructedness.

Step 260 §260.17's correctly-established distinction that a collision-resistant hash is a tamper-detection device, not an identity criterion (two representations may hash differently while denoting the same class); explains empirically why GovernanceLineageNode's integrityHash (Step 267 §267.10) is marked IMPLEMENTED but theory slot unresolved -- hashing and identity are different jobs and the corpus is right not to conflate them.

notations: THEORY GAP / OBSERVABILITY GAP / IMPLEMENTATION GAP / SEMANTIC GAP / REPRESENTATION GAP
note: A five-category classification scheme for theory-vs-implementation mismatches: THEORY GAP (the theory's construct has no design/instance), OBSERVABILITY GAP (the construct exists in schema but reality produces no instances), IMPLEMENTATION GAP (the theory specifies something the schema/code lacks), SEMANTIC GAP (a Type-3 analogy misreported as a Type-1 realization), and REPRESENTATION GAP (a search looked for the wrong class names rather than the right shape); applied across eight named mismatches found in this verification programme.

The only code in the repository literally named 'KnowledgeOs' (scripts/observations/KnowledgeOsDoctor.php, KnowledgeOsInitPlanner.php) is a git-hook/husky installation diagnostic with 10 passing tests, entirely unrelated to the KnowledgeOS theory; zero files in app/ mention KnowledgeState, EpistemicStatus, or even the word epistemic -- meaning a naive codebase search for 'KnowledgeOS' finds an unrelated diagnostic first.

A capstone 30-row falsification table applying an explicit four-class evidence taxonomy (REFUTED: counterexample produced; SURVIVED: strongest test held; UNTESTABLE: cannot be falsified as stated, itself a finding; NOT TESTED: honestly recorded absence) to every major candidate KnowledgeOS claim examined across this gap-discovery programme, scoring 17 refuted (2 conditionally/partially), 11 survived, 2 mixed.

Whether per-assertion 'confidence' in [0,1] as used in the corpus is a genuine probability; executed tests (EXP-7, MT-1/MT-2) show two mutually exclusive per-dimension confidences can sum above 1, demonstrating it is not a probability absent a declared shared (Omega,F,P).

The specific ratified canonical-architecture document (GN-19, 2026-08-28) produced by the falsification-pass-under-authority episode, repeatedly cited across this batch's re-verification programme as the authorized baseline against which raw-corpus (Stratum 1) constructions are measured for adoption status (e.g. I-11 policy stratification, R-1); measured to lack the uncertainty/non-identifiability/missingness constructions present in the raw corpus.

Step 271's principle that a dependency-graph relationship (graph independence) does not establish statistical independence, and any function of graph depth (e.g. IndependenceFactor=1/(1+depth)) must be classified as a structural score rather than an independence measure absent a statistical derivation; later empirically confirmed by exp_measurement.py EXP-6.
